statements.label: supported
statements.text: Within each of the two clades, the cell-to-cell pattern of fate evolution mirrors the pattern of variation found within species.
statements.evidence: Second, we show that this evolutionary pattern matches the pattern of variation within species of each clade.
statements.note: The abstract states that the evolutionary pattern across cells matches the pattern of within-species variation in each clade.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The difference between Caenorhabditis and Oscheius in which cell evolves fastest is caused by a mutation in a single Wnt ligand gene.
statements.evidence: Finally, we propose that the difference between clades is explained by a simple spatial shift across cells of the sensitive region in a Wnt dose-response curve.
statements.note: The abstract proposes a spatial shift of the sensitive region in a Wnt dose-response curve but identifies no gene or mutation behind it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of the six vulval cell fates measured, P3.p fate evolves faster than the others in Caenorhabditis, whereas P4.p is the fastest-evolving cell in Oscheius.
statements.evidence: we quantified the evolution and mutational sensitivity of six cell fates across two clades. First, we find that the cell whose fate evolves fastest is distinct for each clade: P3.p in Caenorhabditis and P4.p in Oscheius
statements.note: Of the six cell fates quantified, the abstract names P3.p as the fastest-evolving in Caenorhabditis and P4.p as the fastest-evolving in Oscheius.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In both clades, cell-to-cell differences in mutational phenotypic variance from random mutation are enough to account for the phenotypic evolution observed.
statements.evidence: Third, we find that within each clade, the differential effect on each cell of random mutation, quantified as their mutational phenotypic variance, is sufficient to explain the observed phenotypic evolution.
statements.note: The abstract reports that, within each clade, the differing mutational phenotypic variance of the cells suffices to explain the observed phenotypic evolution.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: After it became established, tetraploidy opened new genetic routes to adaptation, helping the yeast reach macroscopic multicellular size through the origin of aneuploidy.
statements.evidence: Once established, tetraploidy facilitated novel genetic routes for adaptation, having a key role in the evolution of macroscopic multicellular size via the origin of evolutionarily conserved aneuploidy.
statements.note: The abstract states that established tetraploidy facilitated new adaptive routes, including aneuploidy that underpinned the evolution of macroscopic multicellular size.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Becoming tetraploid gave snowflake yeast longer cells that form bigger clusters, an immediate fitness benefit under selection for multicellular size.
statements.evidence: we found that tetraploidy evolved because it confers immediate fitness benefits under this selection, by producing larger, longer cells that yield larger clusters.
statements.note: The abstract attributes the evolution of tetraploidy to an immediate fitness benefit: larger, longer cells that yield larger clusters.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Tetraploidy in the snowflake yeast arose through mating between diploid cells rather than through genome doubling within single cells.
statements.evidence: we show that diploid snowflake yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) under selection for larger multicellular size rapidly evolve to be tetraploid.
statements.note: The abstract reports that diploid snowflake yeast rapidly became tetraploid but does not say by which cellular route the genome doubled.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Although genomically unstable, tetraploids that arose in the first 50 days were maintained for the next 950 days, close to 5,000 generations, across 10 replicate populations.
statements.evidence: From their origin within the first 50 days of the experiment, tetraploids persisted for the next 950 days (nearly 5,000 generations, the current leading edge of our experiment) in 10 replicate populations, despite being genomically unstable.
statements.note: The abstract reports tetraploids originating within the first 50 days and persisting for the next 950 days, nearly 5,000 generations, in 10 replicate populations despite genomic instability.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The rapid enhancer evolution at pleiotropic developmental genes was driven mainly by positive selection rather than by relaxed constraint.
statements.evidence: We provide evidence that sequence acceleration is associated with turnover of regulatory function.
statements.note: The abstract links sequence acceleration to turnover of regulatory function but does not say whether positive selection or relaxed constraint caused it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Sequence acceleration in one HES1 enhancer produced a new activity domain in the developing limb, which arose together with digit reduction in hoofed mammals.
statements.evidence: Detailed study of one acceleration event in an enhancer of HES1 revealed that sequence evolution led to a new activity domain in the developing limb that emerged concurrently with the evolution of digit reduction in hoofed mammals.
statements.note: The abstract reports that an acceleration event in a HES1 enhancer led to a new limb activity domain that emerged concurrently with digit reduction in hoofed mammals.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Pleiotropic genes involved in gene regulation and development are linked to more enhancers than other genes, which raises their combined enhancer sequence acceleration.
statements.evidence: These genes were connected to more enhancers than other genes, which was the basis for having an increased amount of sequence acceleration over all their enhancers combined.
statements.note: The abstract states that these pleiotropic genes were connected to more enhancers than other genes, which gave them more total sequence acceleration across their enhancers.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Although the genes favoured differed between branches of the mammalian tree, pleiotropic regulatory and developmental genes showed an overall excess of rapid enhancer evolution.
statements.evidence: While different genes and pathways were enriched for regulatory evolution in different parts of the tree, we found a striking overall pattern of pleiotropic genes involved in gene regulatory and developmental processes being enriched for accelerated enhancer evolution.
statements.note: The abstract reports that, despite branch-specific differences, pleiotropic genes in gene regulatory and developmental processes were overall enriched for accelerated enhancer evolution.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The liverwort Marchantia polymorpha lacks stomata, yet a Ia-IIIb bHLH module controls development of its seta, a sporophyte tissue shared by mosses and liverworts.
statements.evidence: in the astomatous liverwort Marchantia polymorpha, a Ia-IIIb bHLH module regulates the development of a unique sporophyte tissue, the seta, which is found in mosses and liverworts.
statements.note: The abstract shows that in the astomatous liverwort Marchantia polymorpha, a Ia-IIIb bHLH module regulates development of the seta.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The Ia-IIIb bHLH module controlled seta development first and was only later co-opted to regulate stomatal formation.
statements.evidence: Our findings reveal the co-option of a Ia-IIIb bHLH TF module for regulating cell fate determination and/or cell division of distinct types of cells during land plant evolution.
statements.note: The abstract reports co-option of the module for distinct cell types but does not say whether its seta role or its stomatal role came first.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: MpSETA, Marchantia's only Ia bHLH gene, and the IIIb bHLH gene MpICE2 both regulate division and/or differentiation of cells in the seta lineage.
statements.evidence: The sole Ia bHLH gene, MpSETA, and a IIIb bHLH gene, MpICE2, regulate the cell division and/or differentiation of seta lineage cells.
statements.note: The abstract names MpSETA as the sole Ia bHLH gene and states that it and MpICE2 regulate division and/or differentiation of seta lineage cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: MpSETA can partly take over the stomatal role of Ia bHLH factors in Arabidopsis, pointing to a conserved mechanism underlying both setal and stomatal formation.
statements.evidence: MpSETA can partially replace the stomatal function of Ia bHLH TFs in Arabidopsis thaliana, suggesting that a common regulatory mechanism underlies setal and stomatal formation.
statements.note: The abstract reports that MpSETA partially replaces the stomatal function of Arabidopsis Ia bHLH factors, suggesting a common mechanism for setal and stomatal formation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In Chironomus riparius, which lacks a cephalic furrow, widespread out-of-plane divisions make the head expand for a shorter time and over a smaller area.
statements.evidence: By contrast, the non-cyclorrhaphan Chironomus riparius lacks cephalic furrow formation and instead undergoes widespread out-of-plane division that reduces the duration and spatial extent of head expansion.
statements.note: The abstract states that Chironomus lacks a cephalic furrow and that its widespread out-of-plane division reduces the duration and spatial extent of head expansion.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: When the cephalic furrow was ablated genetically or optogenetically, compressive stress built up, the head-trunk boundary buckled, and late-stage head and nervous system defects appeared.
statements.evidence: Genetic and optogenetic ablation of the cephalic furrow leads to accumulation of compressive stress, tissue buckling at the head-trunk boundary and late-stage embryonic defects in the head and nervous system.
statements.note: The abstract reports that ablating the cephalic furrow leads to compressive stress accumulation, buckling at the head-trunk boundary and late-stage head and nervous system defects.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: In Drosophila, re-orienting head divisions out of plane also lessens the late-stage nervous system defects that follow cephalic furrow ablation.
statements.evidence: Re-orienting head mitosis from in-plane to out-of-plane in Drosophila partially suppresses tissue buckling, showing that it can function as an alternative mechanical sink.
statements.note: The abstract reports only that out-of-plane head mitosis partially suppresses tissue buckling in Drosophila; it gives no result on late-stage nervous system defects.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study identified two separate cellular mechanisms by which fly embryos keep the expanding head and trunk from colliding.
statements.evidence: We identify two distinct cellular mechanisms that prevent tissue collision between the expanding head and trunk.
statements.note: The abstract states that two distinct cellular mechanisms prevent collision between the expanding head and trunk.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Inside the Fto-containing TAD, the study found circuits for metabolic responses and hibernation-linked cis-elements that make regulatory contacts with nearby genes.
statements.evidence: In this TAD, we uncovered genetic circuits for metabolic responses and hibernation-linked ciselements forming regulatory contacts with neighboring genes.
statements.note: The abstract reports genetic circuits for metabolic responses and hibernation-linked cis-elements contacting neighbouring genes within the Fto TAD.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In hibernating mammals, convergent genomic changes are enriched within particular topologically associated domains, one of which contains the Fto locus.
statements.evidence: Genomic analyses revealed topologically associated domains (TADs) enriched for convergent changes in hibernators, including the Fat Mass & Obesity ( Fto ) locus.
statements.note: The abstract states that genomic analyses revealed TADs enriched for convergent changes in hibernators, including the Fto locus.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Human variants in the hibernation-linked cis-elements of the Fto locus are associated with obesity risk.
statements.evidence: Our findings show how convergent evolution in hibernators pinpoints functional genetic mechanisms of metabolic control, with multiple effects encoded in single CREs.
statements.note: The abstract tests these cis-elements by deletion in mice and reports nothing on human variants or obesity risk.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deleting single cis-elements in mice changed Fto, Irx3 and Irx5 expression in different ways, with distinct effects on metabolism, torpor, obesogenesis and foraging.
statements.evidence: Deletions of individual ciselements in mice differentially altered Fto , Irx3 , and Irx5 expression, reshaping downstream gene expression programs and affecting metabolism, torpor, obesogenesis, and foraging in distinct ways.
statements.note: The abstract reports that single cis-element deletions in mice differentially altered Fto, Irx3 and Irx5 expression and affected metabolism, torpor, obesogenesis and foraging in distinct ways.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In Nymphaea, Nelumbo and Acorus, relative expression differences between homoeologs correlated positively among tissues of each species and among orthologs across all three species.
statements.evidence: Our results show significant positive correlations in RFPKM of homoeologs among tissues within the same species, and among orthologs across these 3 species
statements.note: The abstract reports significant positive correlations in homoeolog RFPKM among tissues within species and among orthologs across the three species.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Homoeologs with balanced expression evolve more slowly in protein sequence than homoeologs with biased expression.
statements.evidence: Our research highlights the importance of balanced expression, shaped by dosage-balance constraints, in the evolutionary retention of homoeologs in plants.
statements.note: The abstract relates expression balance to interactions, lethality scores, retention and regulatory divergence but reports no rates of protein sequence evolution.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Homoeolog pairs with smaller relative expression differences were retained more often after whole-genome duplications in angiosperms.
statements.evidence: Also, homoeologs with lower RFPKM were more likely to be retained after WGDs in angiosperms.
statements.note: The abstract states that homoeologs with lower RFPKM were more likely to be retained after WGDs in angiosperms.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Homoeolog pairs whose expression levels differed less tended to have more protein-protein interactions and higher lethal-phenotype scores.
statements.evidence: Notably, homoeologs with lower RFPKM often had more interactions and higher lethal-phenotype scores, indicating selective pressures favoring balanced expression.
statements.note: The abstract reports that homoeologs with lower RFPKM often had more interactions and higher lethal-phenotype scores.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mice homozygous for null alleles of either Rps27 or Rps27l die, but the two lines die at different developmental stages.
statements.evidence: Furthermore, murine Rps27 and Rps27l loss-of-function alleles are homozygous lethal at different developmental stages.
statements.note: The abstract states that homozygous loss-of-function alleles of Rps27 and Rps27l are lethal at different developmental stages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Producing Rps27 protein from the Rps27l locus, or Rps27l protein from the Rps27 locus, fully rescues the lethality and gives mice without detectable deficits.
statements.evidence: expressing Rps27 protein from the endogenous Rps27l locus or vice versa completely rescues loss-of-function lethality and yields mice with no detectable deficits.
statements.note: The abstract reports that expressing each protein from the other's endogenous locus completely rescues lethality and yields mice with no detectable deficits.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Rps27l-containing ribosomes translate mRNAs of p53 target genes more efficiently than Rps27-containing ribosomes do.
statements.evidence: By endogenously tagging the Rps27 and Rps27l proteins, we demonstrate that Rps27- and Rps27l-ribosomes associate preferentially with different transcripts.
statements.note: The abstract says the two ribosome types prefer different transcripts but neither names those transcripts nor measures translation efficiency.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across mouse cell types, Rps27 and Rps27l mRNA levels are negatively correlated, with Rps27 peaking in lymphocytes and Rps27l in hepatocytes and mammary alveolar cells.
statements.evidence: We show that Rps27 and Rps27l have inversely correlated mRNA abundance across mouse cell types, with the highest Rps27 in lymphocytes and the highest Rps27l in mammary alveolar cells and hepatocytes.
statements.note: The abstract reports inversely correlated mRNA abundance, with Rps27 highest in lymphocytes and Rps27l highest in mammary alveolar cells and hepatocytes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: In predicted complexes, rice de novo proteins bind mainly to other de novo proteins rather than to older proteins.
statements.evidence: Tertiary structure predictions showed that most de novo proteins, though not typically well folded on their own, readily form low-energy and compact complexes with other proteins
statements.note: The abstract says de novo proteins readily form complexes with other proteins but does not say what kind of proteins their partners are.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Per million years on average, random-coil and disordered-region lengths in rice de novo proteins decreased by 8% to 14%.
statements.evidence: In de novo proteins, specifically, we observed an 8% to 14% decay in random coils and intrinsically disordered region lengths and a 2.3% to 6.5% increase in structured elements, hydrophobicity, and molecular recognition features, per million years on average.
statements.note: The abstract reports an average 8% to 14% decay per million years in random coils and intrinsically disordered region lengths of de novo proteins.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Relative to duplicated genes, rice de novo proteins are lighter in molecular weight yet carry more positive charge.
statements.evidence: We also revealed higher positive charges but smaller molecular weights for de novo proteins than duplicates.
statements.note: The abstract reports higher positive charges but smaller molecular weights for de novo proteins than for duplicates.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with gene duplicates, rice de novo genes show faster evolution of disordered regions, secondary structure elements, hydrophobicity and molecular recognition features.
statements.evidence: We found that de novo genes evolve faster than gene duplicates in the intrinsically disordered regions (such as random coils), secondary structure elements (such as α helix and β strand), hydrophobicity, and molecular recognition features.
statements.note: The abstract states that de novo genes evolve faster than gene duplicates in disordered regions, secondary structure elements, hydrophobicity and molecular recognition features.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Rapidly evolving yeast lineages had significantly higher rates of gene loss than their slowly evolving sister lineages, yet also higher speciation rates.
statements.evidence: Faster-evolving lineages (FELs) in yeasts experienced significantly higher rates of gene losses-commensurate with a narrowing of metabolic niche breadth-but higher speciation rates than their slower-evolving sister lineages (SELs).
statements.note: The abstract reports that faster-evolving lineages had significantly higher gene loss rates but also higher speciation rates than their slower-evolving sister lineages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among yeast gene families, those for mRNA splicing, carbohydrate metabolism and cell division were the commonest to be lost.
statements.evidence: Gene families most often lost are those involved in mRNA splicing, carbohydrate metabolism, and cell division
statements.note: The abstract names gene families involved in mRNA splicing, carbohydrate metabolism and cell division as the ones most often lost.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Analysis of 1154 Saccharomycotina genomes showed that yeasts carry fewer genes in total than plants, animals and filamentous ascomycetes do.
statements.evidence: 1154 genomes from nearly all known species in the medically and technologically important yeast subphylum Saccharomycotina. We found that yeast gene family evolution differs from that of plants, animals, and filamentous ascomycetes, and is characterized by smaller overall gene numbers
statements.note: From 1154 genomes, the abstract finds that yeast gene family evolution differs from that of plants, animals and filamentous ascomycetes and is characterized by smaller overall gene numbers.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Rapidly evolving yeast lineages also acquired new gene families at higher rates than their slowly evolving sister lineages.
statements.evidence: Faster-evolving lineages (FELs) in yeasts experienced significantly higher rates of gene losses
statements.note: The abstract compares these lineages only for gene loss and speciation rates and reports nothing about rates of gene family gain.
